name: Bali
catalog_quote: The P-phrase carries a single prominent phrase stress, on the last P-word. Individual P-words earlier in the P-phrase are not perceptibly stressed ... words in isolation are stressed differently from when they occur in phrase: only the phrase-final word carrying stress ... Imposition of phrase-level stress therefore involves the deletion of word-level stress everywhere except in final position.

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three deciding passages (final-syllable rule p.106, suffix shift p.107, phrase-stress/deletion passage p.108) are verbatim in the held Clynes 1995 PDF/txt at the stated pages (PDF pp.123-125). (2) Deciding source: a 393-pp ANU PhD thesis (1995) whose Part I is a full phonology with a dedicated stress section; it is the most detailed first-hand account of Balinese stress that exists — Glottolog lists no later phonology, Ward 1973 is older, Barber/Kersten are dismissed by Clynes himself, and web search found no JIPA Illustration or instrumental study; five open items fetched sources now (Kaufman & Himmelmann draft, Arka 2003 PL-547, Arka & Sedeng 2018, van Zanten & Goedemans 2007, Himmelmann 2018) are all silent or merely consistent. (3) Coding 'final, fixed-dominant, not strict' matches the source. One wording point for the record, not a recode: the correction line says the s

sources.quote: "The stress rule for words uttered in isolation is generally simple: stress the final (rightmost) syllable of the (phonological) word. I could not discern, nor elicit, secondary stresses." (Clynes 1995:106, section 5.8; example on same page: katiwawalan [katiwawa'lan] 'undeveloped jackfruit bud'; p. 107: "The addition of suffixes shifts the stress to the right", jagur-ang [jagu'raŋ], me-jagur-an [majagu'ran])

sources.quote: No phonology chapter. Passing remark on focus prosody: the verb jemak=a with contrastive focus 'has a rising intonation and a strong stress (generally accompanied by vowel lengthening) on the penultimate syllable' (i.e. the stem-final syllable before the enclitic =a, consistent with Clynes p.107 on optionally stressless -a); p.92 disyllabic pronominals ida, ipun, ia 'can be stressed' (consistent with Clynes p.108 'cliticised elements ... attract stress').
